_link.title: I can explain why torque in a DC motor varies as the coil rotates, including the position of maximum and zero torque

toLevel2.stem: At what position of the coil is the torque in a DC motor at its maximum?
toLevel2.answer: When the coil plane is parallel to the magnetic field
distractors: When the coil plane is perpendicular to the field
When the coil is at 45° to the magnetic field
When the coil has completed one full revolution

toLevel2.stem: At what position of the coil is the torque in a DC motor equal to zero?
toLevel2.answer: When the coil plane is perpendicular to the field
distractors: When the coil plane is parallel to the field
When the coil is at 30° to the magnetic field
When the current through the coil is at maximum

toLevel2.stem: Why is the torque zero when the coil plane is perpendicular to the magnetic field?
toLevel2.answer: The forces act directly through the axis of rotation
distractors: No force acts on the coil at this orientation
The magnetic field is zero at this coil position
The current stops flowing through the coil here

toLevel2.stem: What keeps the coil of a DC motor rotating through the zero-torque position?
toLevel2.answer: The angular momentum of the spinning coil
distractors: An increase in current from the power supply
The magnetic field pulling the coil forward
A spring mechanism inside the motor housing

toLevel2.stem: How does the torque on a DC motor coil change during one half turn?
toLevel2.answer: It starts at maximum, decreases, and reaches zero
distractors: It remains constant throughout the entire half turn
It starts at zero, increases, and stays at maximum
It increases steadily throughout the whole half turn

toLevel2.stem: Torque is maximum when the coil is {{blank:1}} to the field and zero when the coil is {{blank:2}} to the field.
At the zero-torque position, the forces on the coil sides act through the {{blank:1}}, producing no {{blank:2}} effect.
The coil carries through the zero-torque position due to its {{blank:1}} {{blank:2}}.
The torque on a DC motor coil is constant throughout its rotation.
distractors: True

toLevel2.stem: Torque is at its maximum when the forces on the coil sides act at the greatest perpendicular distance from the axis.
distractors: False

toLevel3.stem: Why does the perpendicular distance from the axis to each force change as the coil rotates?
toLevel3.answer: Because the coil sides move closer to or further from the axis line of action as it turns
distractors: Because the magnetic field strength varies at different positions inside the motor
Because the current through the coil increases and decreases during each rotation
Because the brushes apply different amounts of pressure at different coil positions

toLevel3.stem: A student observes that a single-coil DC motor runs with a pulsing motion. What best explains this observation?
toLevel3.answer: The torque varies from maximum to zero during each half turn
distractors: The power supply is delivering pulsating direct current output
The brushes are intermittently losing contact with the ring
The permanent magnets are weakening and recovering cyclically

toLevel3.stem: Why do practical DC motors often use multiple coils oriented at different angles?
toLevel3.answer: So that at least one coil always produces significant torque, giving smoother rotation
distractors: So that the magnetic field is stronger at every position inside the motor housing
So that the commutator does not need to reverse the current during each rotation
So that the motor can operate on both AC and DC power supplies simultaneously

toLevel3.stem: At the position of zero torque, forces still act on the coil sides. Why do these forces not produce rotation?
toLevel3.answer: The forces act along a line that passes through the axis, giving zero lever arm
distractors: The forces cancel each other out completely because they are equal and opposite
The commutator disconnects the coil from the supply at the zero-torque position
The magnetic field reverses direction at this position so no net force is produced

toLevel3.stem: How does the torque on the coil change between the parallel and perpendicular positions?
toLevel3.answer: It decreases continuously from maximum to zero
distractors: It stays at maximum until suddenly dropping to zero
It increases continuously from zero to maximum value
It oscillates up and down between the two positions

toLevel3.stem: If the coil of a motor had no mass and therefore no angular momentum, what would happen at the zero-torque position?
toLevel3.answer: The coil would stop because there is no momentum to carry it past the dead point
distractors: The coil would continue rotating because the commutator provides the needed push
The coil would reverse direction because the torque changes sign at this position
The coil would accelerate because zero torque means zero opposition to its motion

toLevel3.stem: As the coil rotates from parallel to perpendicular, the {{blank:1}} arm decreases, causing the torque to {{blank:2}}.
Multi-coil motors produce {{blank:1}} torque because different coils reach their {{blank:2}} torque at different times.
The torque varies because the {{blank:1}} distance from the axis to the line of action of each force changes with the coil's {{blank:2}}.
At the zero-torque position, the forces on the coil sides are also zero.
distractors: True

toLevel4.stem: A motor coil is at 30° from the parallel position. If the maximum torque is 0.12 N m, what is the torque at this angle?
A motor designer adds a heavy flywheel to the motor shaft. How does this affect the motor's performance at the zero-torque position?
toLevel4.answer: The extra angular momentum helps the coil pass smoothly through the dead point
distractors: The flywheel increases the torque at the dead point so the coil accelerates
The flywheel has no effect because torque is independent of the motor's mass
The flywheel causes the motor to stop at the dead point due to extra weight

toLevel4.stem: A student graphs torque versus coil angle for a DC motor. Which description best matches the correct graph?
toLevel4.answer: A sinusoidal curve that is always positive due to the commutator switching
distractors: A straight line that increases steadily with each rotation angle
A constant horizontal line because the commutator keeps torque steady
A series of sharp peaks separated by long intervals of zero torque

toLevel4.stem: Two identical motors are tested: Motor X has one coil, Motor Y has three coils at 60° intervals. Which statement is correct?
toLevel4.answer: Motor Y produces smoother torque because its coils take turns providing peak torque
distractors: Motor X produces smoother torque because fewer coils means less interference
Both motors produce identical torque profiles because they have the same magnets
Motor Y produces weaker torque because the current is split among three coils

toLevel4.stem: At the instant the coil passes through the perpendicular position, the commutator switches the current. Why is this timing critical for maintaining rotation?
toLevel4.answer: If the current were not reversed here, the torque would oppose rotation in the next half turn
distractors: If the current were not reversed, the forces on the coil would increase beyond safe limits
If the current were not reversed, the magnetic field would demagnetise the permanent magnets
If the current were not reversed, the coil would experience maximum torque in both directions

toLevel4.stem: A motor coil rotates at constant angular speed. At what coil position is the rate of change of torque greatest?
toLevel4.answer: Near the perpendicular position where the torque is changing most rapidly
distractors: At the parallel position where the torque is at its peak maximum value
At exactly 45° where force and distance contributions are exactly equal
At the parallel position where the commutator switches the current direction

toLevel4.stem: If the magnetic field in a motor were not uniform but stronger near the edges, how would the torque variation change compared to a uniform field?
toLevel4.answer: The torque would be higher near the parallel position and the variation would differ from a simple sinusoid
distractors: The torque would be constant throughout rotation because the field compensates for position
The torque would always be zero because non-uniform fields cannot produce motor rotation
The torque profile would be identical because only current determines the torque in motors

toLevel4.stem: The torque on a single-coil motor follows a {{blank:1}} pattern that is kept positive by the {{blank:2}}.
Adding more coils at different {{blank:1}} reduces the variation in torque, producing {{blank:2}} rotation.
At 60° from the parallel position, the torque is {{blank:1}} of its maximum value because the lever arm has {{blank:2}} by that factor.

toLevel5.stem: A student argues that a motor with perfectly smooth torque would be more energy efficient. Evaluate this claim by considering the relationship between torque variation and energy loss.
toLevel5.answer: Smoother torque reduces vibrations and mechanical stress, which can reduce energy losses in bearings and structure
distractors: Smoother torque has no effect on efficiency because energy depends only on current and voltage
Smoother torque actually reduces efficiency because constant torque requires more current input
Smoother torque eliminates all energy losses because there is no acceleration or deceleration

toLevel5.stem: Compare the torque profiles of a single-coil motor and a three-coil motor. Which statement best analyses the minimum torque in each case?
toLevel5.answer: The three-coil motor has a higher minimum torque because another coil is always near its peak when one is at zero
distractors: Both motors have the same minimum torque because they use the same magnetic field strength
The single-coil motor has higher minimum torque because all the current goes through one coil
The three-coil motor has lower minimum torque because the current is divided among more coils

toLevel5.stem: A student suggests that using a radial magnetic field (field lines always perpendicular to the coil sides) would eliminate the torque variation. Evaluate this proposal.
toLevel5.answer: Correct; with radial field lines the force always acts at the same perpendicular distance from the axis, giving constant torque
distractors: Incorrect; a radial field would increase the torque variation because the field is now non-uniform
Incorrect; the torque would still vary because the current changes direction with each half turn
Correct; but only because a radial field eliminates the force on the coil sides entirely so torque is always zero

toLevel5.stem: Analyse why a DC motor under heavy load might stall at the zero-torque position but continue running under light load.
toLevel5.answer: Under heavy load the angular momentum may be insufficient to carry the coil through the dead point
distractors: Under heavy load the commutator cannot reverse the current quickly enough for rotation
Under heavy load the magnetic field weakens and cannot produce any force on the coil
Under heavy load the brushes melt and lose contact with the commutator ring surfaces

toLevel5.stem: A physics student plots the instantaneous power output of a single-coil DC motor. Predict the shape of this graph.
toLevel5.answer: It varies periodically, peaking when torque is maximum and dropping to zero when torque is zero
distractors: It is a constant horizontal line because the power supply delivers constant electrical power
It increases linearly with time because the motor continuously accelerates during operation
It is always zero because a single-coil motor cannot produce any net mechanical power output

toLevel5.stem: Explain why the position of maximum torque does not coincide with the position of maximum angular velocity in a single-coil motor.
toLevel5.answer: Maximum torque accelerates the coil, so peak speed is reached later when the torque has dropped
distractors: Maximum torque and maximum speed always occur at the same angular position of the coil
Maximum speed occurs at the parallel position because that is where the force is strongest
Maximum torque slows the coil down, so peak speed occurs when the torque is at its maximum

toLevel5.stem: A student claims that if a motor had zero friction, a single-coil motor would never stall at the dead point. Assess this claim.
toLevel5.answer: Correct; without friction any non-zero angular momentum would carry the coil through the dead point
distractors: Incorrect; even without friction the coil would stop because torque is zero at the dead point
Correct; but only because zero friction means the magnetic field would be stronger at all angles
Incorrect; friction is not related to whether the motor stalls at the zero-torque position

toLevel5.stem: Compare how torque variation affects the design of a motor for a precision instrument versus a motor for a power drill. Which analysis is correct?
toLevel5.answer: Precision instruments need smoother torque and benefit from multi-coil or radial-field designs more than power drills
distractors: Power drills need smoother torque because they operate at higher speeds than precision instruments
Both applications require identical torque profiles because all motors follow the same physics rules
Precision instruments benefit from maximum torque variation because it provides more responsive control

toLevel5.stem: A radial magnetic field ensures the force on each coil side always has a constant {{blank:1}} distance from the axis, producing {{blank:2}} torque.
Under heavy load, a motor may {{blank:1}} at the dead point because the {{blank:2}} is insufficient to carry it through.
